source.title: Open problems on classical de Sitter solutions

accepted.question_text: Do there exist classical de Sitter solutions of 10-dimensional type II supergravity with Op/Dp sources when all sources are parallel and one restricts to the standard smeared ansatz of a 4-dimensional de Sitter spacetime times a compact 6-dimensional group manifold with constant fluxes, or can one prove that no such solution exists?
accepted.context_brief: Parallel-source de Sitter solutions in type II supergravity

evidence.quote: In this paper, we stick to the common ansatz of smeared solutions on group manifolds with constant fluxes; (dis)proving the following conjectures for it is a well-defined question.
Conjecture 1 There is no classical de Sitter solution with parallel sources.
But there is also no proof of this conjecture, despite important constraints on such solutions, summarized e.g. in the introduction of [39].

accepted.question_text: For classical de Sitter solutions of 10-dimensional type II supergravity with intersecting Op/Dp source sets, in the same smeared compactification ansatz on a compact 6-dimensional group manifold with constant fluxes, must every solution be perturbatively unstable in the sense that at least one 4-dimensional scalar mode is tachyonic?
accepted.context_brief: Instability of intersecting-source de Sitter solutions

evidence.quote: In this paper, we stick to the common ansatz of smeared solutions on group manifolds with constant fluxes; (dis)proving the following conjectures for it is a well-defined question.
Conjecture 2 Classical de Sitter solutions with intersecting sources are unstable.

We refer here to a classical, perturbative instability, different than a flat direction or even a metastable case that would be perturbatively stable. In a 4d language, this means that at least one 4d scalar field is at a maximum of its potential, i.e. tachyonic, implying for the standard slow-roll parameter ηV < 0.
Despite various ideas, and studies of concrete examples [16, 27, 28, 31, 32, 34, 35, 37, 39, 40], no analytic proof of this conjecture has been obtained.

accepted.question_text: Can a classical de Sitter solution of 10-dimensional type II supergravity with Op/Dp sources, in the standard smeared compactification ansatz on a compact 6-dimensional group manifold with constant fluxes, simultaneously have large internal volume, weak string coupling, a bounded number of orientifold planes, and quantized fluxes, or is that combination impossible?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we stick to the common ansatz of smeared solutions on group manifolds with constant fluxes; (dis)proving the following conjectures for it is a well-defined question.
Conjecture 3 Classical de Sitter solutions cannot have at the same time a large internal volume, a small string coupling, a bounded number of orientifolds and quantized fluxes.
This conjecture has been recently motivated and studied in [40–42] that considered particular cases or (many) concrete examples, without obtaining a general proof.
